text: {me} of {me.house} storms into the hall: "{suitor} of {rival.house} took my daughter {daughter} from the road at night. Forty riders, no banners. I want her back, and I want his head."

options.label: Order her returned, and {suitor} punished
options.hint: {me.house} +15 · {rival.house} −20 · {rival} will call it the crown meddling in a love match

memory.rival: The King shamed my son {suitor} before the realm.

options.text: By the King's command, {daughter} is returned to {me.house}. {suitor} is sent to the Wall in all but name.

options.label: They are wed. Make it lawful

memory.me: The King blessed the man who stole my daughter.

options.text: The King declares {daughter} and {suitor} lawfully wed. {me} leaves court without a word.

options.label: Let {me.house} take her back by the sword
options.hint: War between {me.house} and {rival.house} · the crown keeps its hands clean
options.text: The King says a {me.father} may fetch {me.his} own daughter. {me.house} calls its banners.

text: {heir}, heir of {me.house}, has run off with a girl of {rival.house}. {me} wants the King's men to bring the young fool home. {rival} says the girl was seduced, and wants blood.

options.label: Bring {heir} home in chains

memory.heir: The King dragged me home in chains.

options.text: The King's riders bring {heir} home in chains. The girl is sent back to {rival.house}, ruined.

options.label: Let love have its way
options.hint: {me.house} and {rival.house} drawn together · both lords −10, both furious
options.text: The King lets the lovers be. Both fathers rage, and slowly, grudgingly, begin to talk.

options.label: Pay {rival.house} for the insult (120 gold)
options.text: The crown pays {rival.house} for its daughter's honour. The matter is closed, on paper.

text: Your spymaster reports that {bannerman}, sworn to {me.house}, was seen at an inn on the border with men in {rival.house}'s colours. Money changed hands. {me} does not yet know.

options.label: Tell {me}

memory.bannerman: Someone told my liege about the inn. I know it was the crown.

options.text: The King sends word to {me}. {bannerman} is summoned to {bannerman.his} liege's hall and does not come out for three days.

options.label: Turn {bannerman} into the crown's spy (80 gold)
options.hint: You will know what {rival.house} plans · if found out, both houses hate you

memory.bannerman: I serve the King now, whoever else I smile at.

options.text: {bannerman} is quietly bought. {bannerman.He} goes on meeting {rival.house}'s men, and now {bannerman.he} tells the King what they say.

options.label: Watch, and say nothing
options.hint: Free · if {bannerman} turns {bannerman.his} coat, {bannerman.his} town goes too
options.text: The King watches. {bannerman} rides home to {me.house}, smiling.

text: A raven intercepted on the Kingsroad: {me} of {me.house} and {friend} of {friend.house} have sworn a pact, sealed with a marriage contract. The letter does not mention the King at all.

options.label: Bless the alliance publicly
options.hint: Both +10 · two houses stand together, for or against you
options.text: The King blesses the pact between {me.house} and {friend.house} before the whole court, as if he had arranged it himself.

options.label: Forbid it
options.hint: Both −15 · the pact is broken, and both lords suspect the other betrayed it
options.text: The King forbids the pact. Each lord is sure the other leaked the letter.

options.label: Warn {rival.house} and let them deal with it
options.text: A copy of the letter finds its way to {rival}. The realm grows tense.

text: {me} of {me.house} asks the King's leave to march on {rivalTown}: "{rival} burns my villages and laughs at your peace. Give me leave, or give me justice."

options.label: Grant leave to march
options.text: The King grants {me} leave to march. The banners of {me.house} go up across the land.

options.label: Forbid it, under pain of treason
options.hint: {me.house} −20 · {me} may march anyway, without your blessing

me.text: settle things with {rival.house} my own way

options.text: The King forbids the march. {me} bows stiffly. No one believes the matter is closed.

options.label: Summon both lords and impose terms (150 gold)
options.text: Both lords kneel at Kingsmere and swear the King's peace. The crown pays for the burned villages.

text: {me} has already sent riders into {rival.house}'s lands. Now {me} asks the King to look the other way: "A small fire, Your Grace. They lit the first one."

options.label: Look the other way
options.hint: {rivalTown} is raided · {me.house} +10 · {rival.house} −15 when they learn of it
options.text: The King looks the other way. {rivalTown} burns, and its men are buried.

options.label: Recall the riders
options.text: The King's herald overtakes {me.house}'s riders on the road. They turn back, cursing.

options.label: Fine {me.house} for breaking the peace
options.text: The King fines {me.house} for its riders. The silver arrives late, and short.

text: {heir}, heir of {me.house}, fell ill at a feast held by {rival.house}. The maester says poison. {me} wants {rival} tried for murder. {rival} swears on the old gods it was bad fish.

options.label: Put {rival} on trial
options.hint: {rival.house} −30 · {me.house} +15 · if innocent, the realm sees a tyrant

memory.rival: The King put me on trial over a sick boy and a bad fish.

options.text: {rival} stands trial at Kingsmere. Nothing is proven. Everything is remembered.

options.label: Send the royal maester to save {heir} (80 gold)
options.hint: {heir} lives · {me.house} +10 · the question is left open

memory.heir: The King's maester saved my life.

options.text: The royal maester rides through the night. {heir} lives, pale and thin, and remembers who saved them.

options.label: Fish is fish

dies.text: {heir}, heir of {me.house}, dies of the fever. {me} names the poisoner in every hall.

options.text: The King declines to act.

text: A boy of fourteen stands in the hall with {bannerman}'s face and none of {bannerman.his} name. {bannerman} asks the King to legitimise him. {me}'s trueborn kin are scandalised.

options.label: Legitimise him

memory.bannerman: The King gave my child a name.

options.text: By royal decree, the boy is trueborn. {bannerman} weeps in the hall.

options.label: A bastard is a bastard
options.text: The King refuses. The boy keeps the name Snow, and {bannerman}'s anger.

options.label: Take the boy into royal service
options.hint: The crown gains a sworn sword · {bannerman} is grateful, and watched
options.text: The boy is taken into the King's service. He swears his oath before the whole court.

text: {me} of {me.house} offers {heir} as a ward at Kingsmere, as a pledge of loyalty. Your council suspects it is a way to plant eyes at court.

options.label: Accept {heir} as ward
options.hint: {me.house} +15 · {me} cannot rise while you hold the child
options.text: {heir} comes to Kingsmere and kneels before the throne. The court watches the newcomer closely.

options.label: The crown needs no pledges
options.hint: {me.house} −10 · a gesture refused is an insult
options.text: The King refuses the ward. {me} takes it as the insult it is.

text: {me} of {me.house} proposes a great tourney at {town} in the King's honour, if the crown puts up the purse.

options.label: Fund the tourney (200 gold)
options.hint: Every house +5 · {me.house} +15 · knights flock to the crown
options.text: The tourney at {town} is the talk of the realm. Two hedge knights win their spurs and swear to the King.

options.label: Let {me.house} pay for it
options.text: {me.house} hosts the tourney at its own expense, and makes sure everyone knows it.

options.label: No time for games
options.text: The King has no time for tourneys. The knights go home disappointed.

text: A sellsword captain, the Golden Wolf, offers five hundred men to whoever pays first. {me} of {me.house} is already bidding.

options.label: Outbid {me} (250 gold)
options.text: The Golden Wolf takes the King's silver. His men camp outside Kingsmere.

options.label: Let {me.house} have them
options.text: The sellswords march under {me.house}'s banner. The other houses count them nervously.

options.label: Banish them from the realm
options.text: The King orders the sellswords out of the realm. They go east, looking for another war.

text: Sickness has come to {town}. {me} of {me.house} wants to close the gates and let it burn itself out. The septons say that is murder.

options.label: Close the gates
options.hint: The sickness stays in {town} · the poor of {town} never forgive

memory.me: I shut the gates of {town} on my own people, with the King's leave.

options.text: The gates of {town} close. For a season, no one goes in or out.

options.label: Send healers and grain (150 gold)
options.text: The crown sends healers and grain to {town}. Some of them do not come back.

options.label: Burn the sick quarter
options.hint: Brutal and certain · {me.house} −10 · the realm whispers about the King
options.text: The sick quarter of {town} burns. The sickness ends. So does the King's name for mercy.

text: {me}, a pious lord, accuses {rival} of {rival.house} of worshipping the old gods in secret: weirwoods, blood, and sacrifices in the night.

options.label: Condemn {rival} as a heretic

memory.rival: The King branded me a heretic on the word of a zealot.

options.text: The King condemns {rival}'s gods. The weirwoods of {rival.house} are cut down.

options.label: Every lord may keep his own gods
options.text: The King declares that every house may keep its gods. {me} prays for the King's soul.

text: A knight of {rival.house} has fled to {me.house} with his whole household, claiming {rival} meant to hang him. {rival} demands him back for trial.

options.label: Let {me.house} keep him
options.text: The knight swears to {me.house}. {rival} sends a raven no one reads aloud.

options.label: Send him back to {rival}
options.text: The knight is returned in chains. He hangs within the week.

options.label: He serves the crown now
options.hint: The crown gains a knight · both −5
options.text: The King takes the knight into his own service, and both lords feel cheated.

text: {me} of {me.house} says {rival.house} never paid the dowry promised in a marriage ten years ago. With interest, {rival.house} owes 200 gold.

options.label: Order {rival.house} to pay
options.text: {rival.house} pays the old dowry. Every coin is counted twice.

options.label: Split the difference
options.text: The King splits the debt down the middle. Neither house is satisfied.

options.label: Ten years is too late
options.text: The King dismisses the claim. {me} mutters about the crown's memory.

text: {bannerman} of {me.house} was killed on a hunt in {rival.house}'s woods. An arrow in the back. {rival}'s men say it was a stray. {me} says it was murder.

options.label: Blood price from {rival.house}
options.text: {rival.house} pays the blood price for {bannerman}. The arrow is never explained.

options.label: Rule it an accident
options.text: The King rules it an accident. {me.house} rides home in silence.

options.label: Send the King's justice to find out (60 gold)
options.hint: Both −5 · the truth comes out, one way or another
options.text: The King's justice finds the bowman. He names no one before he hangs.

text: {me.house}'s harvest is the best in living memory. {me} offers to sell the surplus to the crown, or to the highest bidder across the sea.

options.label: Buy it for the royal granaries (120 gold)
options.text: The King's granaries fill with {me.house}'s grain.

options.label: Tax the windfall
options.text: The King taxes the harvest. {me} pays, and remembers.

options.label: Let them sell abroad
options.text: {me.house}'s grain sails across the sea, and its coffers fill.

text: {bannerman}, sworn to {me.house}, petitions over {bannerman.his} liege's head: "{me} took my best fields for {me.his} own child. I served thirty years. Is this the reward?"

options.label: Rule for {bannerman}

memory.bannerman: The King stood by me against my own liege.

options.text: The King restores {bannerman}'s fields. {me} will not forget who went over {me.his} head.

options.label: A lord's land is his to give

bannerman.text: find a liege who keeps faith

options.text: The King upholds {me}. {bannerman} rides home with nothing.

text: {me} of {me.house} is {me.age} and forgets {me.his} own children's names. {heir} asks the King to let them rule now, before the house is lost.

options.label: Let {heir} rule

memory.me: The King let my own child set me aside.

options.text: The King names {heir} to govern {me.house} in {me.his} name. The old {me.lord} sits by the fire and does not understand.

options.label: A lord rules until death
options.text: The King refuses. {heir} leaves court thinking dark thoughts.

text: Wildlings have crossed into {me.house}'s lands near {town}. Thousands, starving, with children. They say something worse is behind them.

options.label: Let them settle empty land
options.text: The wildlings settle the empty hills by {town}. {me} posts guards on every road.

options.label: Drive them back
options.text: {me.house}'s riders drive the wildlings back into the snow.

options.label: Take their fighters into the King's host
options.text: The wildling fighters swear to the King. Their families go south with them.

text: {rival.house} has raised a toll on the only bridge between {me.house}'s lands and the Kingsroad. {me} calls it robbery.

options.label: Abolish the toll
options.text: The King abolishes the toll. {rival}'s men tear down the gate, slowly.

options.label: The crown takes half
options.hint: The crown gains 80 gold from {rival.house} · both −5
options.text: The toll stays, and the King takes his share. Everyone pays now.

options.label: A lord may toll his own bridge
options.text: The toll stands. {me.house}'s carts take the long way round.

text: Fishermen in {me.house}'s lands have pulled a stone egg from the sea, warm to the touch. {me} offers it to the King. Or to the highest bidder.

options.label: Buy it (200 gold)
options.text: The egg comes to Kingsmere and is set beside the throne. The court swears it moves at night.

options.label: Claim it by right
options.text: The King claims the egg as his right. {me} hands it over with a face like stone.

options.label: Let {me.house} keep it
options.hint: {me.house} +10 · and a house with a dragon egg starts to dream

me.text: hatch the egg, and take the throne

options.text: {me.house} keeps the egg. Its lord has started reading old histories.

text: {rival.house}'s envoy mocked {me}'s dead {me.wife} at a feast in your hall. {me} has demanded satisfaction, and both are reaching for their swords.

options.label: Let them settle it with steel
options.hint: One may die · the winner's house +10
options.text: Steel in the King's hall. The envoy bleeds on the flagstones; {me.house} is satisfied.

options.label: Expel the envoy
options.text: The King expels {rival.house}'s envoy from court.

options.label: Demand an apology from both
options.text: Both men apologise through gritted teeth. The feast does not recover.

text: Silver has been found in the hills near {town}. {me} of {me.house} asks for the mining rights, which by old law belong to the crown.

options.label: Grant the rights
options.text: The King grants {me.house} the silver of {town}. The house grows fat.

options.label: The crown keeps them
options.text: The crown's miners arrive at {town}. {me.house} watches its silver go to Kingsmere.

options.label: Share the silver
options.text: The silver of {town} is shared between crown and house.

text: Forty men deserted the King's levy and are hiding in {town}. {me} of {me.house} will not hand them over: "They are my men first."

options.label: Demand them for hanging
options.text: The deserters are handed over and hanged at the crossroads. The levies stop running.

options.label: Pardon them, back to the levy
options.text: The deserters are pardoned and march back to the King's banner.

options.label: Let {me.house} keep them
options.hint: {me.house} +10 · the King's levy is a joke
options.text: The deserters stay in {town}. Every lord now knows the King's levy is optional.

text: {me} of {me.house} believes {me.his} {me.wife} has taken {rival} of {rival.house} as a lover, and wants the marriage set aside, and {rival} named before the court.

options.label: Grant the annulment
options.text: The marriage is set aside. {rival}'s name is said in every tavern.

options.label: Refuse without proof
options.text: The King refuses. {me} hires men to follow {me.his} own {me.wife}.

options.label: Let the High Septon decide
options.hint: Both −3 · it drags on for years
options.text: The matter goes to the Faith, where it will take years.

text: {me} of {me.house} proposes that {daughter} marry into the royal family. It would bind {me.house} to the crown, and lift it above every other house.

options.label: Accept the match
options.text: {daughter} of {me.house} is betrothed into the royal family. The other houses smile and seethe.

options.label: Decline gently
options.text: The King declines, with gifts. {me} is not consoled.

text: {me} of {me.house} has refused the King's call for levies: "My men are needed at the harvest." Your council says it is a test of your power.

options.label: Send royal troops to collect them
options.text: Royal troops ride into {me.house}'s lands and march the levies out at spearpoint.

options.label: Accept the excuse
options.hint: {me.house} +5 · other houses learn they can refuse
options.text: The King accepts {me}'s excuse. Other lords take note.

options.label: Demand gold in place of men
options.text: {me.house} pays scutage in silver. The King hires his own men.

text: A man of {rival.house} has been caught copying letters in {me}'s solar. Under question he says {rival} sent him to find proof of treason against the crown.

options.label: Investigate {me}
options.text: The King opens an inquiry into {me}. {rival} looks very pleased.

options.label: Hang the spy
options.text: The spy hangs from {me.house}'s walls. {rival} sends no word.

options.label: Feed him false letters and send him back
options.hint: Both houses distrust each other more · the crown watches
options.text: The spy goes home with forged letters. {rival} reads them very carefully.

text: Fire has gutted the lower town of {town}. {me} of {me.house} asks for help to rebuild before winter.

options.label: Rebuild it (180 gold)
options.text: The crown pays to rebuild {town}. New timber rises before the snows.

options.label: Order the other houses to contribute
options.text: Every great house sends silver for {town}. None of them gladly.

options.label: Fires happen
options.text: The King offers his sympathies. {town} winters in tents.

text: {heir} of {me.house} has challenged {rival}'s champion to single combat before the court, to settle the honour of their house.

options.label: Allow the duel
options.hint: {heir} may win great honour, or die

dies.text: {heir} of {me.house} falls in single combat before the court. {me} carries the body home.

options.text: Steel rings in the yard of Kingsmere.

options.label: Forbid it
options.text: The King forbids the duel. {heir} calls it cowardice, within earshot.

text: Ironborn reavers raid {me.house}'s coast near {town}. {me} wants the royal fleet; {me} also wants to know why the crown keeps a fleet at all.

options.label: Send the fleet (150 gold)
options.text: The royal fleet drives the reavers from {me.house}'s coast.

options.label: Let {me.house} build its own ships
options.text: {me.house} raises its own coastal watch.

options.label: Pay the reavers to leave (80 gold)
options.text: The reavers take the King's silver and sail away, laughing.

text: {me} of {me.house} is gravely ill and asks the King to swear, before witnesses, to protect {me.his} house after {me.he} is gone.

options.label: Swear it
options.hint: {me.house} +20 · and you are bound by it

memory.me: The King swore to protect my house.

options.text: The King swears, before the whole court, to protect {me.house}.

options.label: Kind words, no oath
options.text: The King offers comfort, but no oath. {me} understands.

text: {me} of {me.house} brings you a letter: {rival} of {rival.house} invited {me.house} to join a rising against the crown. {me} refused, and came to you.

options.label: Reward {me}'s loyalty (100 gold)
options.text: The King rewards {me.house} publicly. {rival} knows exactly why.

options.label: Strike {rival.house} first
options.hint: War: {me.house} marches on {rival.house} in your name
options.text: The King names {rival} a traitor. {me.house} marches in the crown's name.

options.label: Keep it quiet and watch
options.text: The King thanks {me} and burns the letter. The court never hears of it.
